key_insight: Scale the weight decay coefficient by the learning-rate fraction during training to keep the regularization effect stable without introducing extra asymptotic bias.
engineering_relevance: This gives a near drop-in change for optimizer code that can preserve training stability while speeding up large-scale pretraining, especially for mixture-of-experts models.
method: Replace constant decoupled weight decay with b7/b7_max-scaled decay.
Use RobbinsMonro-style conditions to retain asymptotic stationarity guarantees.
Apply the approach to SGD and the non-Euclidean optimizer Muon (Muon-SW).
evidence_signal: In mixture-of-experts training runs from 72M to 930M parameters, Muon with scaled weight decay reached the same validation loss about 30% faster at the largest scale.
watch_item: The claimed speedup is shown on the reported MoE benchmarks and optimizer setup, so gains may depend on the learning-rate schedule, scale, and implementation details.
paper_title: Scale Weight Decay and Train Better
